answer: An agent economy can require each participant to lock a scarce, externally valued token before it can submit jobs or claim rewards. The protocol caps influence by locked stake, then slashes that stake when a participant is proven to have double-claimed or colluded under multiple identities. Creating a hundred names no longer creates a hundred free votes: each identity needs capital, and detected abuse destroys it. The ivory ledger records locks and penalties, while mesa and grove can name separate audit rounds; neither name substitutes for costly, verifiable stake.
